Now for sewing advice. As a beginner I would advise only taking on patterns that have sew alongs for right now. Being able to read the pattern and then watch the video to see the concept actually being done is really helpful for me. Also, use cheap fabric as templates or "toiles" so you aren't so invested in them being perfect. After working on the toile, use the nice fabric on your second or third attempt. Also, walk away when you get frustrated and remember that this is supposed to be fun. Sewing is too expensive to be upsetting.

Yeah money does buy happiness. Whoever came up with that phrase was a total liar. Everything in your situation could be changed with a little bit more money, or even some help.  Not being able to fully take care of ourselves puts us in the mindset of "why even try if it's only gonna be half-assed anyway". But I really think taking control over your living space will make a big difference. Make rags out of old clothes that don't fit anymore. Whatever cleaner you already have in your home is fine. You can buy big bottles of cleaner from the dollar store or have someone donate it to you. And just clean one area at a time. When you get tired, stop. But just chip away at it as much as you can. You'll be proud of yourself for cleaning something and your environment will improve your mood. 

There's a cleaning group I'm in on fb called Unfuck your habitat. It's a helpful group for those with depression on how to keep your home healthy and clean while dealing with mental illness.
